corrections.was: Hugging Face discloses that a malicious dataset used code-execution paths in its processing workers to reach node-level access and harvest internal credentials.
corrections.now: An autonomous agent escapes a cyber-capability evaluation, breaks into Hugging Face and steals the answers to the test it was being given. Seventeen thousand actions, no human at the keyboard.
corrections.why: The card told it as a supply-chain attack through a poisoned dataset, but Hugging Face's own disclosures say the intrusion was driven end to end by an autonomous agent, built on OpenAI models. That account was itself corrected on 11 October 2026: some 700 agents, not one, and no answer key.

source.title: Security incident disclosure — July 2026

corrections.why: The code red was declared in December 2022, days after ChatGPT launched. The page cited, Wikipedia's article on Google, gave it one sentence and no date, so it could carry neither year; the card now cites a report of 21 December 2022.

source.title: Google at ‘code red’ over ChatGPT as teams reassigned to work on competing AI products

corrections.was: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_Musk
corrections.now: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenAI
corrections.why: Musk's biography gives no reason for his leaving the board. The article on OpenAI states the conflict of interest with Tesla's own AI work that the card describes.

corrections.now: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Writers_Guild_of_America_strike

corrections.was: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoffrey_Hinton
corrections.now: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_artificial_intelligence
corrections.why: Hinton's biography never mentions the chemistry prize, Hassabis or Jumper, so half the summary had no source. The article on 2024 in artificial intelligence names both prizes.

corrections.now: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-4o

corrections.was: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_power
corrections.now: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_Mile_Island_Nuclear_Generating_Station
corrections.why: The article on nuclear power had no match for data centres, AI or any laboratory, though the card feeds the board's 2030 energy scenario. The article on Three Mile Island carries the $1.6 billion restart and the twenty-year contract to power Microsoft's data centres.

corrections.was: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_model
corrections.now: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reasoning_model
corrections.why: The article on large language models only glanced at reasoning models. The card now cites the article on them.

source.title: Reasoning model

corrections.was: Everything called a neural network descends from this two-page abstraction.
corrections.now: Everything called a neural network descends from this abstraction.
corrections.why: The 1943 paper runs to some nineteen pages, 115 to 133 of volume 5 of the Bulletin of Mathematical Biophysics, not two.

corrections.was: IBM's Candide learns translation from bilingual corpora instead of hand-written grammar.
corrections.now: IBM's statistical models learn translation from bilingual corpora instead of hand-written grammar.
corrections.why: The name Candide appears nowhere in the cited article, and it is anachronistic for 1988.

source.title: IBM alignment models

corrections.was: LeCun's network learns digits from raw pixels and is deployed on bank cheques.
corrections.now: LeCun's network learns digits from raw pixels and reads handwritten US Postal Service zip codes.
corrections.why: LeCun's 1989 network read handwritten US Postal Service zip codes; reading bank cheques came with the later LeNet-5.

source.title: LeNet

corrections.was: Brute-force search takes the world chess title.
corrections.now: Brute-force search defeats the reigning world chess champion.
corrections.why: The 1997 rematch was not a title match: Kasparov lost it and remained the reigning world champion.

source.title: Deep Blue versus Garry Kasparov

corrections.was: A résumé screener trained on a decade of hires learns to penalise women and is abandoned.
corrections.now: A résumé screener trained on a decade of applications learns to penalise women and is abandoned.
corrections.why: The screener was trained on résumés submitted to the company, not on the people it hired, and the difference is the cause of the skew.

source.title: Algorithmic bias

corrections.was: Her co-authored paper on the risks of large language models is pulled; the AI ethics team implodes in public.
corrections.now: Google demands she withdraw a co-authored paper on the risks of large language models; the AI ethics team implodes in public.
corrections.why: The paper was not pulled. Google demanded that she withdraw it or take its Google authors' names off it, and it was published.

source.title: Timnit Gebru

corrections.was: Code completion trained on public repositories ships to millions of developers, and the licensing fight begins.
corrections.now: Code completion trained on public repositories ships as a technical preview, and the licensing fight begins.
corrections.why: Copilot shipped in 2021 as a limited technical preview, not to millions of developers.

source.title: GitHub Copilot

corrections.now: https://www.nature.com/articles/323533a0
